To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the commutators involving the generator of a cyclic subgroup of a (m + 2) dimensional Lie group acting on a manifold must take the form [X0, Xj] = −εj X0, where εj = ±1 and that the Jacobi identities imply that the commutator [X0, [X0, Xi]] = 0 for all i.

a Lie transformation group containing a one-dimensional cyclic subgroup must be Abelian if its Lie algebra is of dimension two, and that the Lie algebra of any three-dimensional Lie transformation group containing one-dimensional cyclic subgroup is of Bianchi type I, II, VII0, VIIH, VIII or IX.
a Lie group of transformations containing a one-dimensional cyclic subgroup acting on a manifold has a structure that is considerably more constrained than the structure of a general Lie group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of Lie groups acting cyclically on an n-dimensional manifold.
the classification of Lie groups containing a one dimensional cyclically acting subgroup.
Lie groups which are the symmetry group of some physical system and which contain a one-dimensional subgroup of cyclic symmetry.

all Lie groups compatible with cyclic symmetry have a very simple structure.
the only four-dimensional Lie algrebras compatible with cyclic symmetries are those of Bianchi type I, III, VIIo and VIII.
the structure of the symmetry group is very much restricted by the existence, in the group, of a subgroup acting cyclically.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of the cyclically symmetric groups is severely restricted.
cyclic symmetry imposes strong restrictions on the symmetry group.
the existence of a cyclic subgroup in a Lie group acting on a manifold imposes strong restrictions on the structure and dimension of the group.

, in a Lie algebra compatible with cyclic symmetry, the vector X0 is either a generator of the cyclic group, or is a generator of the Abelian subgroup, or is orthogonal to the cyclic group.
